primary.key: A portion of Mine own Self, transformed in the world of life into an immortal Spirit, draweth round itself the senses of which the mind is the sixth, veiled in matter.
primary.s: Having named his supreme abode, from which none return, Krishna turns to the embodied soul; Śaṅkara (Advaita), Gītā Bhāṣya 15.7, reads this portion as a portion only in imagination, like the sun reflected in water, which returns to the sun once the water is removed.
primary.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 15.7, trans. A. Mahadeva Sastri, 2nd ed. (1901), archive.org bhagavadgitwith00agoog

basis.words: He is like the sun reflected in water ; the reflected sun is but a portion of the real sun ; and on the removal of water the reflected sun returns to the original sun and remains as that very sun. … Our theory is not open to this objection ; for, it is only a portion limited by the up^dhi sjet. up by avidy^ ; it is a portion as it were, an imaginary portion.
basis.gloss: He [the individual soul] is like the sun reflected in water: the reflected sun is only a portion of the real sun, and when the water is removed the reflected sun returns to the original sun and remains that very sun. … [To the objection that the partless Supreme Self can have no portion:] our view is not open to this objection, for it is only a portion limited by the limiting adjunct (upādhi) set up by ignorance (avidyā): a portion as it were, an imaginary portion.

standby.key: Since I excel the destructible, and am more excellent also than the indestructible, in the world and in the Veda I am proclaimed the Supreme Spirit.
standby.s: After setting the Supreme Self apart from the destructible and the indestructible, Krishna claims that place as his own; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), Gītā Bhāṣya 15.17 to 15.18, reads the two he surpasses as the souls still bound and the souls set free.
standby.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 15.17 to 15.18, trans. A. Govindacharya (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

basis.words: But there is a Supreme Soul (or Spirit) Who is different from both Kshara and Akshara, or Conditioned souls and Freed souls, respectively. That Spirit is declared as a distinct Postulate, as the Paramatma, in all the Srutis. The very epithet Param-atma (the Supreme or Exalted Soul) shows that the Supreme Spirit is a distinct Verity other than the bound and the freed souls. … Inasmuch as, for reasons stated aforesaid, | am beyone the Kshara-soul—described—and transcend also the Akshara-soul—the musta, described—thence), I am renowned as Purushottama—the Sublimest Purusha.
basis.gloss: [On 15.17:] There is a Supreme Soul who is different from both the Kshara and the Akshara, that is, from the conditioned souls and the freed souls respectively; he is declared in all the Śrutis as the Paramātman, and that very name shows the Supreme Spirit to be a reality distinct from the bound and the freed souls. … [On 15.18:] Since, for the reasons given, I am beyond the Kshara soul already described and transcend also the Akshara soul, the freed (mukta) soul, I am renowned as Purushottama, the highest Person.
